- Errand, QA, and reviewer helper threads are read-only for repository files; specialists may write under `.agents/`. Writers retain full worktree access. Wait backstops report helper edits as `repo_edited` with changed files and do not revert them.
- Full plugin backups use a versioned JSON payload (`kind: 'bb-project-folders-backup'`, version 1) containing settings and all 11 durable tables: folders, folder_paths, thread_places, folder_rules, project_rules, project_order, execution_defaults, session_policies, preferences, item_styles, and folder_archives. Imports preserve row IDs and run in one transaction; invalid backups and imports during an active move or archive are rejected. Transient tables (exports, pending_exports, project_moves, thread_moves, section_moves) are excluded. This adds no schema changes and preserves the existing appearance-only export/import flow.
- An owner's approved goal authorizes reversible steps in their own accounts. Ask once for consent covering any destructive, paid, outgoing, permission-changing, or irreversible steps.

{"summary":"This task contract ('council-office-live') transforms the Council room into an always-on isometric pixel-art 3D office powered by three.js, displayed simultaneously with a retro pixel-styled history log and a message-by-message replay system. The council page must display both the office canvas and the history log at all target viewports (375px, 768px, and 1280px) without any view toggles. All visual states are derived client-side from the existing CouncilDetail data structure; no backend RPC or server-side changes are permitted, and packages/council/ is strictly read-only.

The core architectural changes involve three new or modified UI modules:
1. 'src/rooms/council/ui/office-behaviour.ts': Exports pure state derivation logic including deriveOfficeActors(detail, cursor, now), nextWanderTarget(rng, current, points), and seatColor(id). Actors represent seats, chair, and owner (if owner spoke). In live mode or replay cursor, the speaking actor stands at the central meeting table with a speech bubble (first words of message or '…' while generating). When replying, the actor turns to face the answered seat. When inactive (terminal council state or 20s without speaking), actors wander between predefined office locations (coffee corner, desks, bookshelf, plants) unless prefers-reduced-motion is enabled.
2. 'src/rooms/council/ui/council-office.tsx': Implements the CouncilOffice component. It lazily loads three.js via dynamic import, detects WebGL support, and renders a graceful text fallback if WebGL is unavailable without throwing errors. It builds an isometric pixel-art scene using flat geometries and CSS-based pixel filtering (no external textures or sprites). On unmount, it disposes all Three.js renderers, scenes, geometries, materials, and animation frames.
3. 'src/rooms/council/ui/council-page.tsx': Restructures the page layout to host the office canvas alongside the dialogue log. Log entries are styled as retro pixel dialogues with square avatars colored via seatColor(id). Clicking a log entry highlights the speaker in the office with its speech bubble. Adds replay controls (play, pause, step) that advance a cursor through message sequences, driving both the 3D office actors and auto-scrolling the log. The composer buttons are restyled as pixel buttons while preserving existing RPC actions (council_say, decide, council_stop).
4. 'packages/i18n/src/i18n.ts': Adds localized strings in English and Russian for replay controls (play, pause, step) and the WebGL fallback message.
5. Tests: 'tests/council-office.test.ts' verifies actor derivation across live and replay states as well as wander target selection.
